topic: Andrew Wiles's 1995 Annals of Mathematics paper 'Modular elliptic curves and Fermat's Last Theorem' (with the companion Taylor–Wiles paper) proving Fermat's Last Theorem
Appel and Haken's 1977 Illinois Journal of Mathematics proof that every planar map is four colorable (computer-assisted)
Thomas Hales's 2005 Annals of Mathematics proof of the Kepler conjecture on sphere packing density pi/sqrt(18)
The 2017 Forum of Mathematics, Pi paper 'A formal proof of the Kepler conjecture' (Flyspeck project) giving a machine-checked proof
Georg Cantor's 1874 Crelle paper showing the real numbers cannot be put in one-to-one correspondence with the natural numbers (algebraic numbers are countable)
Paul Cohen's 1963 PNAS paper 'The independence of the continuum hypothesis'
Kurt Gödel's 1938 PNAS note on the consistency of the axiom of choice and the generalized continuum hypothesis
Agrawal, Kayal and Saxena, 'PRIMES is in P' (Annals of Mathematics 2004): primality testing in deterministic polynomial time
Green and Tao 2008 Annals of Mathematics: the primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions
Yitang Zhang 2014 Annals of Mathematics: bounded gaps between primes (infinitely many prime pairs differing by less than 70 million)
Rivest, Shamir and Adleman 1978 Communications of the ACM: a method for obtaining digital signatures and public-key cryptosystems
Diffie and Hellman 1976 IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 'New directions in cryptography' (public-key distribution)
Cooley and Tukey 1965 Mathematics of Computation: an algorithm for the machine calculation of complex Fourier series (FFT)
Ferdinand Lindemann's 1882 Mathematische Annalen paper proving that pi is transcendental
David Hilbert's 'Mathematical Problems' lecture (Paris 1900) as published in English in the Bulletin of the AMS in 1902
Maryna Viazovska 2017 Annals of Mathematics: the sphere packing problem in dimension 8 (E8 lattice is optimal)
Preda Mihăilescu 2004 Crelle: primary cyclotomic units and a proof of Catalan's conjecture (8 and 9 are the only consecutive perfect powers)
The Clay Mathematics Institute's 2010 announcement awarding the Millennium Prize for the resolution of the Poincaré conjecture to Grigoriy Perelman
The NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions definition of the gamma function as Euler's integral (DLMF 5.2.1)
Gregory Chaitin's 1966 Journal of the ACM paper on the length of programs for computing finite binary sequences (algorithmic information)
